title: Verdant 12 — Scarp Tileset for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled & Godot: 16x16 Elevation
tagline: 414 tiles at 16x16. Elevation that reads at sixteen pixels, 7 complete 47-mask sets, MZ, Tiled and Godot importers.
description:
414 tiles at 16x16. 7 complete 47-mask autotile sets, 18 objects, and the feature this series cut once and deferred for months: terrain that reads as being at two different heights, at sixteen pixels.

Elevation, and why it took this long

A cliff is not hard to draw. It is hard to make read, and the reason turns out to be arithmetic rather than art. Whether a raised surface reads as raised depends on how far its tone sits from the ground below, measured against how much the ground’s own texture already varies. A nineteen-tile cliff set was drawn for this series and cut after six iterations, every one of them reading as a trench — and measured from the pixels those tiles actually emitted, the cause was not the cliff at all: its wall body sat at the same brightness as the grass it stood in, a separation of 0.004 against a floor of 1.0.

So this pack chooses its value structure before it draws anything. The lowland meadow is two adjacent greens with every brighter mark kept sparse, which holds its whole tonal swing to 25 levels of brightness. Against that, the sunlit upland cap scores 3.11 and the shadowed scarp face 1.33. Both clear the floor, the pair that was cut is kept as a negative control in the same function, and every one of those numbers is computed from the emitted pixels of the tiles in this download rather than from a colour table.

The scarp then gets the four things that say “vertical”: a lit lip where the turf turns over, a rock face below it, a dark plinth at the foot, and a shadow cast on the grass. That is four cues in the four rows a 16-pixel cell affords.

What is in it

  • 7 complete 47-mask autotile sets — the plateau scarp with its face, plinth and cast shadow; the talus fan at its foot; a drove road on both levels; bracken on both; and a boundary onto Verdant 01 Overworld’s original grass so a buyer of both can run one map into the other.
  • 24 terrain fills — four variants each of lowland meadow, sunlit upland turf, shadowed scarp face, loose talus, packed earth track, rust bracken.
  • 18 objects, 61 prop tiles — every one ships transparent and already grounded on the surface it belongs on, with the contact shadow between the two.
  • A finished sample map, as a PNG, as editable JSON that rebuilds that PNG byte-for-byte, and as a Tiled .tmx you can open and change.

329 of 414 tiles — 79% — are transitions. A landscape is mostly boundaries, and a terrain pack without them is a swatch book.

Three engine importers, and what checked each one

A shipped importer is a claim about a program we do not run. The only honest way to hold it is to run it, so each of these was verified by making the engine itself count and measure.

  • RPG Maker MZ — a full A2 autotile sheet at 48px, the sheet MZ’s own autotile brush paints with rather than a page of loose stamps. 48 ÷ 16 = 3, an integer, so the upscale is pure pixel replication with no resampling. Every shape MZ can request is composed back out of the sheet using the engine’s own FLOOR_AUTOTILE_TABLE, parsed from the runtime, and compared byte-for-byte.
  • Godot — the shipped .tres was loaded headless in Godot 4.7.2 and Godot itself was made to COUNT: all 414 tiles built, every atlas source resolved, every footprint exact. Headless load and resource inspection only — not the editor GUI, not a TileMapLayer, not a running game.
  • Tiled — every shipped .tsx was opened and rendered by Tiled 1.10.2’s own tmxrasterizer and compared to the sheet you download, tile by tile. The .tmx sample map renders pixel-for-pixel identical to the shipped PNG: 614,400 pixels compared, 0 differ.
  • Anything else — Unity, GameMaker, LÖVE and custom engines get the loose PNGs, the packed sheets and tiles.json.

What is proven, and what is not

  • Exact grid — every one of the 414 tiles is a whole number of 16x16 cells, and every sheet a whole multiple of it. Checked in both directions.
  • Palette lock — every opaque pixel is one of the 51 declared colours. Not “mostly”: every pixel. That is what makes tile 414 match tile 1.
  • No anti-aliasing — alpha is strictly binary. No halo, no soft upscale, no resampling anywhere in the pipeline.
  • Autotile completeness — all 7 sets carry all 47 masks, 329 slots, enumerated against the mask table rather than counted by hand.
  • Sheets match the loose tiles — the same art ships twice on purpose, and all 414 were compared and are identical.

⚠ Seamlessness is NOT claimed. Every tile’s wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4×4 repetition is rendered and reviewed — the fields ship in proof/repetition/ so you can look for the grid line yourself. That is a measured floor and a human review, not a proof: a statistical wrap test catches hard edge artefacts about 97% of the time and the commonest real defect only about 7%, because that defect damages the very interior the test calibrates against. A weaker true claim beats a strong false one.

AI disclosure

The graphics are generated programmatically, by a procedural pixel-art engine written for this series — there is no diffusion model and no training dataset involved in producing a single pixel. The generator’s source code was written with AI assistance, and this listing carries the platform’s Generative AI tag on that basis.
